importance.critical: Near-monopoly / single-source / breaking this link breaks the chain
importance.major: Large $$ flow + few alternatives; meaningful slowdown if disrupted
importance.meaningful: Real revenue exposure but with substitutes available
importance.tangential: Real but small / highly diversified on at least one side

single_source_risk.high: 1 dominant supplier, no near-term substitute (multi-year + multi-billion to replicate)
single_source_risk.medium: 2-3 viable suppliers; switching cost real but bounded
single_source_risk.low: Many suppliers; commoditized or easily dual-sourced
single_source_risk.none: Buyer has internal alternative or true commodity

schema.annual_usd_billions_note: Rough estimates based on disclosed segment revenue, IR commentary, analyst consensus, and PPA disclosures. Specific contract values are seldom public; ranges given where precision is uncertain. Treat as order-of-magnitude, not contract value.

TSM->NVDA.what_flows: Advanced-node foundry capacity (4N/3nm/2nm) + CoWoS-L/S advanced packaging for Hopper/Blackwell/Rubin AI GPUs
TSM->NVDA.deal_basis: Est. NVDA spent ~$25-30B at TSM in 2024, growing toward ~$40-50B in 2026 as Blackwell ramps; TSM HPC segment ~58% of total revenue and NVDA is its largest HPC customer.
TSM->NVDA.alternatives: Samsung Foundry (3nm yields uncompetitive for HPC), Intel Foundry (18A unproven for AI workloads). No production alternative for CoWoS at scale.
TSM->NVDA.trend: Growing fast; CoWoS-L packaging capacity is the hard bottleneck on NVDA shipments through 2026.
TSM->NVDA.key_event: TSM Arizona Fab 2 expected to begin Blackwell production H2 2026 — first NVDA US-fabbed AI GPUs.

TSM->AMD.what_flows: 3nm/4nm foundry + CoWoS packaging for MI300/MI325/MI350 + EPYC CPUs
TSM->AMD.deal_basis: AMD second-largest HPC customer at TSM after NVDA; CDNA/Zen 5 fabbed exclusively on TSM.
TSM->AMD.trend: Growing with MI350 ramp; AMD competing with NVDA for limited CoWoS capacity.

TSM->AAPL.what_flows: Apple Silicon (M-series + A-series) on TSM's most advanced node every year
TSM->AAPL.deal_basis: Apple historically takes the entire first run of TSM's leading node (N3, N2). ~20-25% of TSM revenue.
TSM->AAPL.trend: Stable; Apple commits to N2 in 2025-26.

TSM->AVGO.what_flows: Custom AI ASICs for hyperscalers (GOOG TPU, META MTIA), networking ASICs (Tomahawk/Jericho), VMware compute
TSM->AVGO.deal_basis: AVGO's AI segment (~$20B+ FY25) is mostly custom ASIC silicon fabbed at TSM N3/N5.
TSM->AVGO.trend: Growing fast on TPU + custom AI ASIC volume.

TSM->QCOM.what_flows: Snapdragon mobile + auto silicon on N3/N4

TSM->MRVL.what_flows: Custom AI ASICs (AMZN Trainium, MSFT Maia successors), DSPs for optical interconnect

ASML->TSM.what_flows: EUV scanners (NXE:3800E, NXE:3600D) + high-NA EUV (EXE:5000) for sub-7nm logic. ~$200M per scanner, ~$300M+ for high-NA.
ASML->TSM.deal_basis: TSM is ASML's largest customer. ~30-35% of ASML system revenue.
ASML->TSM.alternatives: None. ASML has 100% global EUV monopoly. No substitute exists.
ASML->TSM.trend: Growing with high-NA EUV adoption for 2nm/A14 nodes.
ASML->TSM.key_event: TSM took delivery of first high-NA EUV in 2024 for A14 development.

ASML->SSNLF.what_flows: EUV scanners for Samsung Foundry advanced nodes + memory (DRAM 1z/1a)
ASML->SSNLF.trend: Stable but constrained by Samsung's logic foundry yield issues.

ASML->INTC.what_flows: EUV + high-NA EUV for Intel 18A and A14P (foundry strategy)
ASML->INTC.trend: Largest high-NA orders to date; INTC was ASML's first high-NA EUV customer.

AMAT->TSM.what_flows: Deposition (CVD/PVD/epi), ion implant, CMP, advanced packaging tools
AMAT->TSM.alternatives: LRCX (etch+CVD overlap), TEL (Tokyo Electron, foreign-listed only)

LRCX->TSM.what_flows: Plasma etch + ALD/CVD for advanced logic and 3D NAND
LRCX->TSM.trend: Growing with advanced packaging + NAND layer counts.

KLAC->TSM.what_flows: Wafer & reticle inspection + metrology — near-monopoly in process control
KLAC->TSM.alternatives: Limited (ONTO Innovation for some metrology niches)
KLAC->TSM.trend: Growing with high-NA EUV yield management complexity.

SHECY->TSM.alternatives: SUMCO (SUOPY) is the only meaningful #2; combined SHECY+SUMCO = ~60% global supply.
SHECY->TSM.trend: Stable; capacity constrained but new fabs (Yamaguchi expansion) in 2026.

LIN->TSM.what_flows: On-site industrial gases — neon (excimer laser fuel), helium, ultra-pure N2/H2/O2
LIN->TSM.alternatives: APD on-site at some fabs; AIQUY (Air Liquide) in Europe.
LIN->TSM.trend: Stable; helium supply diversified post-2022 Russia/Ukraine shock that hit neon.

APD->TSM.what_flows: On-site industrial gases — same role as LIN at other fabs

SNPS->NVDA.alternatives: CDNS (Cadence) head-to-head competitor; most chip design teams use both.
SNPS->NVDA.trend: Growing with chip complexity + AI-assisted design (Synopsys.ai).

CDNS->NVDA.what_flows: EDA tools + IP (HBM controllers, advanced node sign-off)
CDNS->NVDA.trend: Growing with AI workloads + Cadence.ai stack.

ARM->AAPL.what_flows: CPU architecture license (perpetual, fixed-fee) + royalties on M-series + A-series
ARM->AAPL.alternatives: Apple has architecture license; could theoretically switch to RISC-V but committed to ARM ISA.
ARM->AAPL.trend: Stable; ARM v9 royalty rate is higher.

ARM->QCOM.what_flows: Architecture license (under dispute) + chip royalties for Snapdragon
ARM->QCOM.key_event: Nuvia-related licensing dispute mostly resolved 2024-25; royalties stable.

ARM->NVDA.what_flows: ARM v9 architecture for Grace CPU + Cosmos CPU + ARM Neoverse-based DPU
ARM->NVDA.trend: Growing as NVDA platform includes more CPU+GPU integrated systems.

MU->NVDA.what_flows: HBM3E + HBM4 for AI GPUs — Micron is the #3 HBM supplier (after SK Hynix + Samsung)
MU->NVDA.deal_basis: MU has multi-year HBM3E/HBM4 supply agreements with NVDA. ~$10-12B of MU FY26 revenue attributable to AI HBM.
MU->NVDA.alternatives: SK Hynix (#1, KRX-only public), Samsung (SSNLF OTC).
MU->NVDA.trend: Growing fast; MU gaining share in HBM4. Sold-out through 2026.
MU->NVDA.key_event: MU first to qualify HBM3E 12-Hi for B200 in early 2025.

MU->AMD.what_flows: HBM3E + DDR5 for MI300/MI350 + EPYC servers

NVDA->SMCI.what_flows: H100/H200/B100/B200/B300 GPUs as system components in SMCI's GPU server SKUs
NVDA->SMCI.deal_basis: SMCI FY25 (Jun 2025) revenue ~$22B; ~85% of that is GPU systems, of which most is NVDA-based. xAI Colossus + CoreWeave + hyperscalers.
NVDA->SMCI.alternatives: AMD MI300 for ~10% of SMCI's GPU revenue.
NVDA->SMCI.trend: Volatile (Q4 FY25 supply timing); structural demand intact.

NVDA->DELL.what_flows: H100/H200/B100 GPUs as PowerEdge XE9680/XE9712 components for enterprise + hyperscaler
NVDA->DELL.deal_basis: DELL ISG AI server revenue ran ~$5B/qtr in late FY25, ~70% NVDA GPU pass-through.
NVDA->DELL.trend: Growing fast; DELL is NVDA's largest enterprise channel.

NVDA->HPE.what_flows: GPUs for Cray AI supercomputers + ProLiant
NVDA->HPE.trend: Growing with HPE Cray supercomputer wins (Aurora, etc.).

NVDA->MSFT.what_flows: Direct + via DELL/SMCI: H100/H200/B100/B200/B300 for Azure AI clusters supporting OpenAI

NVDA->MSFT.alternatives: Maia 100/200 (MSFT internal silicon via TSM); AMD MI300 small share.
NVDA->MSFT.key_event: Stargate $500B AI infra commitment announced Jan 2025.

NVDA->META.deal_basis: META disclosed plans for ~350K-400K H100s by end-2024; capex run-rate ~$60-70B in 2025-26 with majority on AI infra.
NVDA->META.alternatives: MTIA (Meta's custom AI silicon via TSM); slow ramp.

NVDA->GOOGL.what_flows: H100/H200/B100/B200 for GCP customer-facing AI + Gemini training (alongside Google TPU)
NVDA->GOOGL.alternatives: Google TPU v5/v6 (via AVGO + TSM) — internal alternative.
NVDA->GOOGL.trend: Mixed; GOOGL increasingly TPU-first for Gemini.

NVDA->AMZN.what_flows: H100/H200/B100/B200 for AWS customer-facing AI (Bedrock, P5/P6 instances) alongside Trainium
NVDA->AMZN.alternatives: Trainium2/3 (AMZN custom silicon, via MRVL + TSM).
NVDA->AMZN.trend: Growing on NVDA side and on Trainium side.

NVDA->TSLA.what_flows: H100 cluster for FSD model training (Cortex datacenter)
NVDA->TSLA.trend: Stable; TSLA had ~35K H100s and growing.

NVDA->ORCL.deal_basis: ORCL-OpenAI deal Sep 2025: $30B in compute commitments over 5yr, requiring large NVDA buildouts.
NVDA->ORCL.trend: Growing fast; ORCL was a structural ramp story 2025-26.

COHR->NVDA.what_flows: 800G + 1.6T optical transceivers for NVDA Spectrum-X AI fabrics + Mellanox-derived networking
COHR->NVDA.trend: Growing fast; AI fabric is COHR's #1 growth driver.
